messages:
eva_ops: Heads up — production inference in us-west-2 is seeing big perf regressions this morning. Jobs on the mixed H100/L40 pool are 4-6x slower and some are timing out. Seeing a lot of NCCL fallbacks to SOCKET in the logs.

chris_infra: Oof. Any logs/snippets? Is this coincident with the kernel/driver rollout we did last night?

eva_ops: Pasted a short excerpt from the pod logs (truncated):
```
I NCCL 2026-05-12 08:12:11.123456 NCCL INFO NCCL P2P: NVLINK peer map mismatch detected
I NCCL 2026-05-12 08:12:11.123789 NCCL WARN NCCL P2P/SHM check failed (errno=22)
I NCCL 2026-05-12 08:12:11.124000 NCCL INFO NET/Socket transport selected as fallback
E RUN 2026-05-12 08:12:35.876543 Allreduce failed: timeout
```

maria_sre: That looks like the usual mixed-sku detection problem where NVLINK peer masks differ across driver/kernel combinations. Which driver/kernel went out?

chris_infra: We rolled kernel 6.6.11 + nvidia-driver 540.2 on a subset of hosts last night (canaries), and auto-rolling started hitting the mixed pool around 07:40 UTC. Some older hosts are still on 535.104 + kernel 6.4.x.

devon_ml: Confirming: the scheduling placed training shards across hosts with different driver stacks. When NCCL can't establish a consistent NVLINK topology it falls back to TCP, which explains the latency spike.

eva_ops: I also grabbed `nvidia-smi topo -m` from two nodes (one H100, one L40):
```
Node A (H100, driver 540.2):
GPU0 GPU1 CPU Affinity ...
GPU0 NVLINK  20 GB/s to GPU1
GPU1 NVLINK  20 GB/s to GPU0

Node B (L40, driver 535.104):
GPU0 PCIe    12 GB/s to GPU1
GPU1 PCIe    12 GB/s to GPU0
```
So topo looks different between nodes.

maria_sre: That mismatch is the culprit. NCCL expects consistent P2P capabilities when forming cross-host rings; mixed NVLINK/PCIe characteristics can trigger fallback logic.

chris_infra: Short-term mitigation options: 1) Evacuate workloads off hosts with driver 540.2 and keep them on homogeneous pools (H100-only / L40-only). 2) Pin training jobs to same host set via nodeAffinity. 3) Roll back the driver on the canaries to 535.104.

eva_ops: We tried pinning but autoscaler still placed some shards on different node groups. Evacuating whole hosts is easiest operationally but costs capacity and may increase job queue times.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-05-12-1789 — "NCCL P2P fallbacks causing large latency regression in us-west-2 mixed-pool" — Pager duty routed to eng-infra + ml-platform.

maria_sre: Temporary action plan: A) Pause further driver rollouts to other regions (chris). B) Add a cluster-level node taint for 540.2 hosts so scheduler avoids mixed placement (eva/devon). C) Start a targeted rollback of driver 540.2 on the 6-8 affected hosts if tainting isn't quick enough (chris). D) Run end-to-end smoke tests on a small cross-host allreduce to confirm.

chris_infra: I'll pause the rollout now and push a taint via daemonset that marks nodes with driver=540.2: `kubectl taint nodes <node> nvidia-driver=540:NoSchedule` — should be quick. If that doesn't fully drain we will rollback the driver.

devon_ml: We need to communicate to customers — this impacts dedicated H100/L40 mixed pools in us-west-2 only. Estimated additional hours-to-complete for queued jobs: +3-6 hours if we keep tainted pool offline. Cost impact estimate: ~$6k/day if we run extra reserve capacity while we stabilize. (ballpark)

maria_sre: Postmortem owners and checkboxes: chris = rollback/rollout pause, eva = tainting + drainage strategy, devon = customer comms & perf numbers, maria = root-cause analysis and NCCL config recommendations.

eva_ops: One more note — we observed a couple of nodes reporting `shmget: permission denied` in dmesg which might explain SHM check failures. Could be a kubelet seccomp/profile or a recent cgroup setting change with the new kernel. I'll add that to the RCA list.

chris_infra: Good catch. I'll run `dmesg | tail` on the affected hosts and share logs in this thread. If SHM is blocked we may need a kubelet config tweak instead of rollback.

maria_sre: For future resilience, let's add a scheduler predicate that avoids mixing driver-major versions for jobs that need P2P by default. We'll treat this like an SLO-risk change.

eva_ops: Thanks team — starting the taint now and will update when drainage begins. :thumbsup:
